_comment: Recall of our own relevance filter over the pools in ./fixtures-pool, which are captured BEFORE the filter runs. Regenerate deliberately (node scripts/reportPoolRecall.mjs --write-baseline) and review the diff — a floor that falls means the matcher started discarding products it used to keep. Never re-baseline to make a red build green.
_floorsComment: Per-query floors, so a change cannot raise the mean by helping easy queries while destroying one. A low floor can still mean the LABELS are generous rather than the filter wrong — freilandeier counts any plain egg — so read a floor against goldenSet.ts before raising the matcher to chase it.
_labelCorrectionComment: 2026-08-06: meanRecall 0.871 -> 0.867, obst 1.00 -> 0.916, ruebli 0.265 -> 0.150. NONE of this is the filter discarding products it used to keep — read it before treating it as the regression this file otherwise describes. The labels were corrected in goldenSet.ts and the DENOMINATORS moved with them, so the filter's verdict is now being scored on the right set of products. obst: 15 labelled relevant -> 24, because Aprikosen, Datteln, Feigen, Nektarine, Pfirsich, Pflaumen, Physalis, Passionsfrucht, Pitahaya and Sultaninen had been unjudged, while Hipp baby cereal, two Früchtequarks and three fruit bars had been counted as fruit. ruebli: the corpus had been counting Rüebli biscuits, a Rüebli cake, a carrot-orange-ginger juice and Betty Bossi marzipan carrots as the vegetable. TWO REAL DEFECTS THE OLD LABELS HID, both now visible and both left unfixed on purpose so that a ground-truth correction and a matcher change are never in the same diff: (1) 'Obst' drops Migros 'Sultaninen' — raisins are dried grapes — and that one product is the whole 0.084; (2) far worse, 'Rüebli' keeps the biscuits and the cake and DROPS almost every actual carrot (Karotten, Snack Karotten, Baby Karotten, Erbsen und Karotten, all Migros). The old 0.265 looked like a merely weak query; it was the filter inverting the query. Both are written up in the tracker as the next matcher work.
